name: Fibril-fold dementia test
subtitle: names a dementia by its proteins' shape

effects.effect: flash-frozen molecules can be imaged atom by atom with electrons
crystals build themselves from identical repeating units

effect: flash-frozen molecules can be imaged atom by atom with electrons
how: Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and other dementias look alike early on yet need different drugs, and they are often told apart for certain only after death. A drop of spinal fluid is mixed with fresh protein so any misfolded seeds copy their exact fold onto it, growing fibres the way a crystal copies itself; the fibres are flash-frozen and imaged atom by atom, and each disease's fibres have their own tell-tale cross-section.
obstacle: Fibres grown in a test tube often take a different fold from the ones in the brain, which would give wrong answers.
why: Cryo-EM proved each dementia has its own fold, but only in brains after death.
real: Seeded amplification plus cryo-EM distinguished PD from MSA fibrils, but from post-mortem brain tissue; living-patient diagnosis remains a proposal.
